text: Before starting a Duel, you must have a deck(s). There are 3 kinds of decks:
• Main Deck (must contain 40 - 60 cards): This deck contain all of your mainly used cards including Monsters, Spells, Traps,...
• Extra Deck (must contain 0 - 15 cards): This deck contain monsters that can be only Special Summoned. Those monsters can bring a huge advantage to your tactics.

• Side Deck (must contain 0 - 15 cards): For normal Duel, you don't need a Side Deck, but in standard Match which includes 3 Duels, after finish the first Duel, you will want to alter the contents of the Main Deck and Extra Deck to duel with opponent's deck(s). Therefor, you will need a Side Deck that contain cards which has special uses.
Notice:
Extra Deck and Side Deck are optional, so you can still play without them.
After altering your Main Deck / Extra Deck, the number of cards in each decks must remain the same
A Yu-gi-oh Duel is conducted on a playmat, like the following one:
Deck Zone & Extra Deck Zone: Each players have 2 zones to place their Main Deck and Extra Deck. For Side Deck, player can place it an anywhere else.
Monster Zones: Where monsters are placed and battling.
Spell & Trap Zones: Where spells, traps are placed and activated.
Pendulum Zones: The leftmost and rightmost Spell & Trap Zones are also Pendulum Zones which used for placing Pendulum Monsters.
Field Zone: The zone used for placing Field Spell.
Graveyard Zone (GY): The zone of used, destroyed or discarded cards.
Extra Monster Zones: Two player share 2 Extra Monster Zones, although Main Monster Zones can also hold monsters from Extra Deck, but for Link Monsters, those must be placed in Extra Monster Zones.
Each player start with 8000 LP (Life Points). Whoever can reduce opponent's LP to 0 (by battling, or effects...) wins the Duel, if both players' LP become 0, it will be treated as a draw.
A player's turn will include the following phases:
• Draw Phase: The turn player draw 1 cards from their Main Deck.
• Standby Phase: A transitional phase between the Draw Phase and Main Phase 1.
• Main Phase 1: The turn player can summon monster, activate or set spells, traps,...

• Battle Phase: Battle Phase: During this phase, turn player's monsters can attack and battle with your opponent's monsters. Unlike other phases which player must enter, player can choose to skip the Battle Phase.
• Main Phase 2: The same as Main Phase 1. If player skipped Battle Phase, the Main Phase 2 won't happen, of course...
• End Phase: The turn ends.
There are 4 types of summoning in Yu-gi-oh:
• Normal Summon: Place monster from hand to Main Monster Zones vertically and face-up.
• Set: Place monster from hand to Main Monster Zones horizontally and face-down.
• Flip Summon: When a monster is already Set, player can flip it up (place it vertically face-up in the same zone). But, a monster cannot be flipped in the turn it was Set.

• Special Summon: A type of summon which requires a special method or under specific conditions (can be placed either vertically or horizontally, face-up or face-down, by default, special summoned monsters must be face-up).
Notice:
Player can only Normal Summon or Set 1 monster once per turn, but can Flip Summon as many as possible if there is enough Set monsters.
There no limit for the times of Special Summon.
First, let's learn about Battle Position - it is the way that monsters was placed in the field:
• Attack Position: A monster is in Attack Position if it is placed vertically and face-up.
Face-up Defense Position: A monster is in Face-up Defense Position if it is placed horizontally and face-up.
• Face-down Defense Position: Monsters that was Set.
Of course, a monster can't attack unless it is in Attack Position. When a monster attack another monster. There can be 3 situation:

• If both are in Attack Position: Which monster with lower ATK will be destroyed (and sent to GY). The owner also lose LP equal to the ATK difference. If 2 monsters have the same ATK, both will be destroyed and players take no damage.

• If attacked monster is in face-up Defense Position: If attacking monster's ATK is less than attacked monster's DEF, it won't be destroyed, but the owner still lose LP equal to difference. If attacked monster's DEF less than attacking monster's ATK, it will be destroyed, but the owner won't lose any LP.
● If attacked monster is in face-down Defense Position: It must first be changed to face-up Defense Position, the rules will be apllied like the same above.
